newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: NSW YOUNG DOCTORS REJECT TALKS OFFER
New South Wales' junior doctors have rejected an offer by the Federal Health Minister for discussions if they abandon their statewide strike.
AMA spokesman for junior doctors, Doctor Brian Owler, says they're not interested in Dr Wooldridge's offer to talk about the implementation of legislation restricting Medicare Provider numbers.
He says there've been three requests for a meeting with the minister which have been ignored.
Meanwhile junior Doctors in the Northern Territory will join their New South Wales counterparts today for an indefinite strike.
REDS PLAYERS RATED HIGHLY BY BENNETT
In Rugby League, two of the Perth Reds contenders for representative teams this year have been praised by Queensland and Brisbane Broncos coach, Wayne Bennett.
Rodney Howe and Jon Grieve were strong performers in the Reds 26 to 16 loss yesterday against the Broncos in Perth.
Bennett says he rates both very highly.
Grieve is in the Queensland provisional squad for the tri-series against New South Wales and New Zealand, while Howe is expected to be named in the Blues squad.
WA LIBERAL'S WRANGLING TO CONTINUE
Wrangling within the West Australian Liberal Party is set to drag on for at least another three weeks, with the selection process to fill a Senate vacancy starting all over again.
Over the weekend, the Liberal's State Council overturned its endorsement for Upper House M-P, Ross Lightfoot.
Mr Lightfoot had been a controversial choice, and when it was revealed that ousted Senator, Noel Crichton-Browne, had helped secure the numbers, the Party was once again bitterly divided.
It's understood that Mr Lightfoot lost his ratification by only two votes, setting the scene for another round of public wrangling between those groups for and against Mr Crichton-Browne.
Fresh nominations will be called today, and candidates will have until Friday to declare whether they will contest the race or not.
The Party will decide on April the 5th and 6th who will fill the vacancy caused by the death, in January, of Senator John Panizza.
CALLS FOR INQUIRY INTO NUCLEAR REACTOR ISSUES
The Australian Democrats and the New South Wales Liberals want the future of the Lucas Heights nuclear facility in Sydney, and the location of a new reactor, to go before an Inquiry.
The Federal Government hs denied a press report that the Lucas Heights facility might be shut down, and a new reactor built at Jervis Bay on the New South Wales south coast.
The report suggests Cabinet will consider the move as part of a deal to build Sydney's second airport at Holsworthy, in the south-west.
Democrats Environment Spokeswoman, Meg Lees, says the reported reactor proposal is aimed at diverting debate away from the airport site controversy.
She says it's time the government was open about its plans for the Lucas Heights reactor, and whether Holsworthy is still under consideration as an airport site.
WA POLICE HUNTING SERIAL KILLER
Western Australian police fear a serial killer is on the loose, and say they're committing every resource to hunt down the killer, believed to be stalking young women in Perth.
Twenty-seven-year-old Ciara (KEER-uh) Glennon is the third woman to vanish from outside nightspots in the Perth suburb of Claremont in the past 15 months.
Ms Glennon was last seen in the early hours of Saturday morning.
Commander Bob Ibbotson, of the State Crime Squad, says Ms Glennon's dissappearance is similar to that of Sarah Spiers, who is still missing, and Jane Rimmer, who was murdered.
SENATE TO DEBATE REEF CHARGES
The Senate will tomorrow debate increased charges for visitors to the Great Barrier Reef, after last year's budget contained a five dollar per visitor increase.
The tourism industry has been lobbying hard to have it scrapped, claiming the levy will keep tourists away from the reef.
After a strong backlash, the Government agreed to split the increased charge, implementing a one dollar increase from last January, with the remaining five dollars to come into effect next January.
The Tourism Council of Australia's written to senators pointing out problems created by the increased charge, and its concern the revenue isn't being used directly for the protection of the reef.
TOURISM LOBBY AGAINST REEF TAX RISE
Tourism Council of Australia Queensland manager, Daniel Gschwind, has written to all federal senators urging them to reject an increase in the Great Barrier Reef tax.
Mr Gschwind says the system is a mess and is affecting the businesses that have to collect the charge and the tourists who have to pay it.
The federal government intends to increase the Environmental Management Charge with a one dollar increase from last January and a four dollar rise from next January.
The Senate is scheduled to debate the increase tomorrow.
USS KITTYHAWK ARRIVES IN HOBART
The American aircraft-carrier, USS Kittyhawk, has arrived in Hobart for a five day good-will visit.
The Kittyhawk has fifty-five-hundred officers and crew aboard and up to three thousand will be taking shore leave everyday.
The 80-thousand tonne ship is returning to it's San Diego base from a three-month tour of duty in the Persian Gulf, monitoring the no-fly-zone over Northern Iraq.
The Kittyhawk's Battle Group Commander, Rear Admiral Peter Long, says the task was "tense" and the crew are keen to relax in Hobart.
The ship is anchored off Kangaroo Bluff, which is about one nautical mile from the Hobart wharves.
